verdicts.correction: Bars are short pixel sets along correlation-recovered lines, fixed before any tree is fitted. The exact-line fraction grows with n (L=2: 0.33/0.38/0.42) and depends strongly on how often the centre pixel is inked: on qd_dev L=2 it rises from 0.08 to 0.81 between the least and most inked quartile of centres. verdicts.note: Checks used the training rows and the npz. (1) 'Stroke templates' is interpretation: bars come from the correlation ranking, so their straightness is a property of the construction and the data, not of the booster. (2) 'Within 1 px' is a weak criterion for 5-pixel sets; it is 0.957 already at n=1000 and does not move with n. (3) Confound: corr(centre ink frequency, straight) is +0.56 (L=2) and +0.48 (L=4) on qd_dev n=10000. Predicting gain-weighted straightness from ink-frequency-quartile composition alone gives 0.303 vs measured 0.323 at L=4 (all bars 0.244), and 0.506 vs measured 0.432 at L=2. The claim's evidence cites only qd_dev L=4 and leaves out the null L=2 result (0.379 vs 0.379 at n=3000; 0.432 vs 0.421 at n=10000).

verdicts.correction: In each of the six runs (seed 0) cgbt has the lowest out-of-fold error of all members. verdicts.note: 'Takes over ggbt's role' is measured against v2 only at qd_dev n=10000. cgbt and ggbt agree on 0.92-0.98 of test points. The convex stacker splits weight between these two near-collinear members on one 2000-row holdout, so 'ggbt dropped' is a property of one fit. Boosters early-stopped on error give over-confident log-probabilities (clipped at 1e-5), while ET, logistic regression and kNN votes are smoother, so equal weights do not mean equal influence.

verdicts.correction: Bars are two thirds of cgbt's columns (0.658 on QuickDraw/MNIST, 0.667 on Fashion). With LightGBM sampling 12% of columns per tree, they carry 0.72-0.80 of its split gain on QuickDraw and MNIST, 1.09-1.22 times their column share. On Fashion they carry 0.60, below their column share (0.90x). Per column, the 9-pixel bars (1.40-1.65x) and, on QuickDraw, the 16-pixel pooled sums (1.51-1.85x) carry the most gain. The 5-pixel bars carry less than the average column everywhere (0.73-0.90x). In ggbt the 300 pairs (about 10% of its columns) carry 0.38-0.41 of the gain, 3-4x their column share; the exception is qd_a's out-of-fold fit at 0.30. Split gain is training-loss reduction at the best iteration and is shared arbitrarily among overlapping features (each L=2 bar is a subset of an L=4 bar; pooled sets overlap bars). It describes how the trees split, not what the predictions depend on.
verdicts.note: Column shares come from the n fields of the booster gain records in the analysis JSONs. The L=4/L=2 ratio (1.7-2.2x, 1.4x Fashion) is fair because the two have equal column counts. The MNIST and qd_a ggbt values come from out-of-fold fits (7998 and 8000 rows). 'About 40%' needs '(0.30 on qd_a)'.

verdicts.correction: With each subset sum's TreeSHAP contribution (to the class's own raw score) spread equally over its pixels, 0.56-0.69 of cgbt's net contribution falls on pixels blank in the point (mean over classes; 0.15-0.92 by class). Blank pixels make up 0.55-0.83 of those same images (qd_dev 0.745, qd_a 0.734, MNIST 0.825, Fashion 0.546 of the 784 pixels), so per pixel, inked pixels carry more of the evidence on QuickDraw and MNIST, and Fashion is at par. ggbt's subset-sum features give similar shares (0.53-0.68). ggbt's lower overall share (0.39-0.44) comes from the pair spreading rule, which puts pair contributions only on inked pixels by construction. Because a partially inked subset sum's contribution is split by member count, these shares cannot separate evidence from absent ink from evidence from present ink.
verdicts.note: Recomputed on the same 100 points per class (rng 1, streamed from the cached data). (1) 'Each class' is false: grapes 0.35, soccer ball 0.32, campfire 0.39 (qd_dev); pullover 0.25, shirt 0.28, coat 0.29 (Fashion); camouflage 0.15 (qd_a); digit 8 0.42 (MNIST). (2) On the bars, among (point, bar) cases with at least one inked member, 43% (L=2) / 52% (L=4) of the members are blank on qd_dev (MNIST 43/54%, Fashion 19/24%). About half of a partially inked bar's contribution is therefore booked as blank, even when the bar's ink drove it. (3) 'Rely on blank pixels about equally' is largely built in, since both boosters' non-pair features are equal-spread subset sums over overlapping footprints. (4) The maps contain no ablation or occlusion test, so they make no causal statement.

verdicts.correction: In the mean contribution maps (seed 0, n=10000, 100 test points per class, contributions to the class's own raw score), the regions chosen after looking at the maps take large shares. Ocean: the horizon ends (0.17/0.21) and, for cgbt, a diagonal band (0.26) where ocean has less ink (0.134) than the other classes (0.258; most in soccer ball 0.37, campfire 0.33, grapes 0.30, washing machine 0.29). Per-class ink in the ocean band, from class_mean: frying pan 0.199, below the other-class mean, so 'round classes (soccer ball, frying pan, washing machine)' is partly wrong. The segment-vs-blob contrast is a consequence of the feature shapes, not a learned property; only which segments carry weight is informative. The C7 caveat applies: 'empty' regions' shares include contributions of features that are partly inked. 'MNIST 0 = the empty hole' overstates a 46% share.

verdicts.correction: Pair gain is concentrated: the top 10 of 300 pairs carry 0.29 (qd_dev), 0.50 (Fashion) and 0.36 (MNIST) of the pair gain, against 0.033 if gain were uniform. other_problems: §2.2 and fig_img_gain.pdf give gain shares without the column-share reference: bars are 2/3 of cgbt's columns, pairs about 10% of ggbt's, and LightGBM uses feature_fraction 0.12 per tree. Readers will take 'bars carry three quarters of the gain' as dominance, but it is 1.1-1.2x the column share on QuickDraw/MNIST and 0.9x on Fashion. Add column shares, or gain per column.

fig_img_stack.pdf annotates raw stacker weights (e.g. cgbt 0.34 at qd_dev n=10000), while the text and tables quote shares of total weight (0.470) for the same quantity. Neither shows influence, because the weights act on log-probabilities of different calibration.

§2.3 reading 'on MNIST the horizontal bars are favoured, in places where a horizontal stroke or gap tells digits apart' does not fit the top bars. MNIST's top L=2 bar (centre (1,18), 1.02% of cgbt's gain) has pixels inked (x>0.1) in 0-7.5% of training images. The (25,12) L=4 bar lies on row 25 (2-10% inked), and the (19,24) L=2 bar's pixels are inked in 1-4%. These look like detectors of the digit's extent in the margins, not of strokes.

§3 calls the TreeSHAP contributions to the true class's own raw score in a multiclass softmax 'evidence' for the class. That is not the margin over competing classes, and with no occlusion or ablation test nothing shows a region is necessary. The 'Measured' paragraphs should say this.

§3.4 and §3.1 'both boosters use mostly the same places' (map correlation 0.63-0.94): cgbt and ggbt share the raw pixels and all pooled-sum features, and both use the same spreading rule, so some of this agreement is built in.

§5.3 'cgbt is a better booster than ggbt (lower out-of-fold and test error at every n measured)': on qd_a and MNIST the test comparison pits ggbt's 8000-row out-of-fold fit against cgbt's 10000-row fit. Only the out-of-fold comparison is like-for-like.

§0 says out-of-fold differences at n=10000 have s.e. about 0.008 (unpaired). For member-vs-member comparisons on the same 2000 rows the paired s.e. is much smaller. Say which is meant, and note that the stacker weights are fitted on the same holdout.
img_far_members.md defines 'inked' as x>0, while the contribution maps and regions use x>0.1. State both definitions where the ink frequencies are quoted.
fig_img_contrib_qd_dev.pdf labels the ggbt row 'ggbt (v2 run)', but the text says the maps come from the v3 fits. They are identical, so this is harmless but inconsistent.
Gain-weighted bar statistics (straightness, orientation) rest on few bars: the top 10% of bars carry 0.65-0.86 of the bar gain. They come from one seed and one fit, and need that qualifier.
